name: Darius I
title: King of Persia who rebuilt the temple
summary: Darius I (Darius the Great) was the Persian king who reigned from about 522 to 486 BC. He played a crucial role in biblical history by confirming Cyrus's original decree regarding the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem and ordering that work should continue after a period of stoppage. During his reign, the second temple was completed in 516 BC.

keyEvents.title: Temple construction halts and the matter is brought before Darius
keyEvents.description: Opponents of the Jews tried to stop the rebuilding of the temple. The case was sent to King Darius for a decision.

keyEvents.title: Darius confirms Cyrus's decree
keyEvents.description: Darius ordered a search in the royal archives and found Cyrus's original decree allowing the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Darius orders that the temple construction shall continue
keyEvents.description: Darius issued a new decree ordering that work on the temple should continue without hindrance, and that costs should be covered by the royal treasury.

keyEvents.title: The temple is completed during Darius's reign
keyEvents.description: The second temple was completed in the sixth year of Darius's reign, to great joy for the Jewish people who had returned from exile.

keyEvents.title: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah prophesy during Darius
keyEvents.description: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah encouraged the people to resume temple construction in the second year of Darius's reign, with God's promises of blessing.

keyEvents.title: Haggai brings God's promise of glory in the new temple
keyEvents.description: During Darius's reign, Haggai prophesied that the new temple would surpass the former one in glory, and that God would bless his people.
